clue.text: Speak softly and carry a (T. Roosevelt)

definitions.text: Speak softly and carry a (T. Roosevelt)

parts.words: Speak softly and carry a (T. Roosevelt)
parts.note: the clue quotes Theodore Roosevelt's maxim about diplomacy and stops just short of the final two words, which the solver supplies

explanation.surface: A quotation from Theodore Roosevelt left hanging before its last words.
explanation.walkthrough: Roosevelt's saying runs 'Speak softly and carry a big stick; you will go far': the missing words are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The completed proverb names a cudgel held in reserve, Roosevelt's image for threatened force behind quiet diplomacy.

explanation.definitionFit: The study of plants is a branch of science, and the same word names Botany Bay in New South Wales.

explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of chemistry, one branch of science, is called by this title.

clue.text: Source of the Bs of S "and all our woe, with loss of Eden"

definitions.text: Source of the Bs of S "and all our woe, with loss of Eden"

parts.words: Source of the Bs of S "and all our woe, with loss of Eden"
parts.note: the quotation is from the opening lines of Milton's Paradise Lost, about the forbidden fruit eaten in Eden, here also the origin of all branches of science

explanation.surface: Milton's lament for the Fall, applied to the origin of all science.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's lines tell of the fruit 'of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste brought death into the world, and all our woe'. 'Bs of S' means branches of science.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the forbidden fruit came from the tree whose eating brought knowledge, the root of all learning and of mankind's fall.
